answer: At most 1 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a island tag. The jetty cap is enforced at intake and harbor publishes the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool hence cannot mint a farm in one epoch however much capital it holds, because each member consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 3 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
